source_text:
κόσιν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τὸ παντὸς ἔργου λοιπὸν ἀπέχεσθαι σαρκικοῦ, καὶ τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς σπουδασμάτων καὶ εἰκαίου περιφορᾶς, ἀποπεραίνειν δὲ μᾶλλον ἐπείγεσθαι μόνα τὰ εἰς ζωὴν ἀποφέροντα τὴν ἀκήρατον, καὶ ὅσα σεπτοὺς καὶ ἁγίους ἀποτελεῖ. Ὡς γὰρ ὁ σοφὸς ἡμῖν γράφει Παῦλος, «Ὁ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸς κατέπαυσεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ, ὥσπερ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων ὁ Θεός.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές.
{ΚΥΡ.} Ὧδε μὲν οὖν τὸ θεῖον ἔφη χρησμῴδημα ἡμῖν. Εἰσηγούμενος δὲ τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ τὸ κεκελευσμένον ὁ θεῖος ἔφη Μωσῆς, «Ἀπελθόντες λάβετε ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς πρόβατον κατὰ συγγενείας ὑμῶν, καὶ θύσατε τὸ Πάσχα. Λήψεσθε δὲ δέσμην ὑσσώπου, καὶ βάψαντες ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ παρὰ τὴν θύραν θήσετε ἐπὶ τῆς φλιᾶς, καὶ ἐπ' ἀμφοτέρων τῶν σταθμῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος, ὅ ἐστι παρὰ τὴν θύραν. Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐξελεύσεσθε ἕκαστος τὴν θύραν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ, ἕως πρωΐ. Καὶ παρελεύσεται Κύριος πατάξαι τοὺς Αἰγυπτίους, καὶ ὄψεται αἷμα ἐπὶ τῆς φλιᾶς, καὶ ἐπ' ἀμφοτέρων τῶν σταθμῶν, καὶ παρελεύσεται Κύριος πρὸς τὴν θύραν, καὶ οὐκ ἀφήσει τὸν ὀλοθρευτὴν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὰς οἰκίας ὑμῶν πατάξαι.» Τὸ μὲν οὖν κατ' οἴκους πατριῶν ἤτοι κατὰ συγγενείας λαμβάνεσθαι τὸν ἀμνὸν, ὑποφήνειεν ἂν, οἶμαί που, τῆς πνευματικῆς οἰκειότητος τὸ, ὡς ἐν πίστει τε καὶ ὁμονοίᾳ ταυτόν. Οὐ γὰρ τοῖς ἐξίτηλα φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις συνεορτάσομεν, οὐδὲ τοῖς ἕτερα ἄττα παρά γε τὸ ὀρθῶς ἔχον καὶ ἀληθῶς φρονεῖν εἰωθόσι κοινωνήσομεν τῆς ἁγίας καὶ ζωοποιοῦ θυσίας, ἀλλὰ τοῖς ὁμόφροσί τε καὶ ἀδελφοῖς ὡς ἐν ἑνότητι πνεύματος, καὶ ἐν ταυτότητι πίστεως. Ἀναπλέκεταί γε μὴν ἡ ὕσσωπος οἰκονομικῶς τῷ αἵματι τοῦ ἀμνοῦ. Καὶ τίς ἂν γένοιτο καὶ τοῦδε τυχὸν ὁ λόγος, ὡς ἐν βραχέσιν ἐρῶ. Τὴν ὕσσωπον, ὦ Παλλάδιε, πόαν εἶναί φασι καὶ δὴ καὶ ἰατρῶν θαυμάζουσι παῖδες, ὡς οὐκ ἀνικάνως ἔχουσαν εἴς γε τὸ δύνασθαι καὶ μάλα γεννικῶς τὴν ἐν σπλάγχνοις ἐκτήκειν ἀκαθαρσίαν, καὶ καταλεπτύνειν εὖ μάλα τὰ τῶν φλεγμάτων συμπεπηγότα, διάτοι τὸ τῆς ἐνούσης αὐτῇ φυσικῆς θερμασίας εὐσθενές. Συνῆπται δὴ οὖν, καθάπερ ἔφην ἀρτίως, τῇ ὑσσώπῳ τὸ αἷμα, πλαγίως ἡμῖν τοῦ τύπου σημαίνοντος, ὡς οὐ μόνον ἡμᾶς ἀπαλλάττει φθορᾶς, τὸ τίμιον αἷμα Χριστοῦ, ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ ἁπάσης ἀκαθαρσίας, τῆς εἰς τὸ εἴσω κεκρυμμένης, καὶ ἀποψύχεσθαι μὲν οὐκ ἐᾷ πρὸς τὸ ῥᾴθυμον, ζέοντας δὲ μᾶλλον ἀποτελεῖ τῷ πνεύματι. Ὅτι δὲ ἀναγκαῖον καὶ λυσιτελὲς, τοῖς γε ἅπαξ ἠξιωμένοις μεταλαχεῖν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τὸ ἀσφαλῆ τε καὶ ἀνεξίτητον ποιεῖσθαι φιλεῖν τὴν ἐν ἁγιασμῷ ζωὴν, ὑποσημαίνει πάλιν ὁ νόμος, εἴσω καθίζων θυρῶν τοὺς τὸν ἀμνὸν κατεδηδοκότας, ἵνα μὴ τοῖς Αἰγυπτίοις συνολοθρευθεῖεν, τῶν οἴκων ἐκβεβηκότες. Ἐνδοιάσαι γὰρ οὐ θέμις, ὡς ἀπαστισοῦν τῶν τελούντων ἐν ἡγιασμένοις, οἶκον ὥσπερ τινὰ τὴν ἀρε
pass_a_gloss: (For it would be fitting for those having entered by faith) into the rest of Christ, thereafter to abstain from every fleshly work, and from the zeals on earth and vain going about, and rather to be eager to complete only the things bearing toward the undefiled life, and whatever makes people revered and holy. For as wise Paul writes to us: The one having entered into his rest, and it is plain that (it is the rest) of Christ, himself also rested from his works just as God from his own. PALLADIUS: True. CYRIL: Thus then the divine oracle spoke to us. And introducing to those from Israel the thing commanded, divine Moses said: Having gone away, take for yourselves a sheep according to your kinships, and slay the Passover. And you will take a bundle of hyssop, and having dipped from the blood the one beside the door, you will put on the lintel and upon both the posts from the blood which is beside the door. And you will not go out, each the door of his house, until morning. And the Lord will pass by to strike the Egyptians, and will see blood upon the lintel and upon both the posts, and the Lord will pass by toward the door and will not let the destroyer go into your houses to strike. Now the lamb being taken according to houses of fathers or according to kinships would show, I suppose somewhere, the sameness of spiritual belonging, as in faith and like-mindedness. For we will not feast together with those who have chosen to think faded (debased) things, nor will we share the holy and life-making sacrifice with those used to thinking some other things than what holds rightly and truly, but with those of the same mind and brothers, as in oneness of spirit and in sameness of faith. Indeed the hyssop is entwined economically (by design) with the blood of the lamb. And what the reason of this too might be, I will say in brief. Hyssop, O Palladius, they say is a plant, and indeed the children of doctors marvel at it, as not being incapable of being able very vigorously to melt out the uncleanness in the entrails, and to thin out very well the congealed masses of phlegms, on account of the vigor of the natural heat being in it. So the blood is joined, just as I said just now, to the hyssop, the type signifying to us obliquely that the precious blood of Christ releases us not only from corruption but also from every uncleanness hidden toward the inside, and does not allow us to grow cold toward laziness, but rather makes us boiling in the spirit. And that it is necessary and useful for those once deemed worthy to partake of Christ to love to make secure and not departed-from the life in sanctification, the law again hints, seating inside the doors those who have eaten the lamb, so that they may not be destroyed together with the Egyptians, having gone out of the houses. For it is not lawful to doubt that whoever at all of those counted among the sanctified, having as a sort of house the vir(tue) (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: … into the rest of Christ, from then on to keep away from every work of the flesh, from earthly pursuits and idle running about, and to hasten instead to accomplish only what leads to the undefiled life and makes people venerable and holy. For as the wise Paul writes to us, ‘Whoever has entered his rest’ (that is, clearly, Christ’s) ‘has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his own’ (Hebrews 4:10).

Cyril: This, then, is what the divine oracle told us. And when the divine Moses was laying the command before the sons of Israel, he said, ‘Go and take for yourselves a sheep according to your families, and sacrifice the Passover. And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in some of the blood that is by the door, and put it on the lintel and on both doorposts, some of the blood that is by the door. And none of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning. And the Lord will pass by to strike the Egyptians, and he will see the blood on the lintel and on both doorposts, and the Lord will pass by the door, and he will not let the destroyer come into your houses to strike’ (Exodus 12:21–23).

That the lamb is to be taken by fathers’ houses, that is, by families, would indicate, I think, the sameness of spiritual kinship, as in faith and in concord. For we shall not keep the feast together with those who have chosen to hold perverted views, nor shall we share the holy and life-giving sacrifice with those accustomed to think things other than what is right and true, but with those who are of one mind with us and are our brothers, as in unity of spirit and in sameness of faith.

The hyssop, moreover, is joined by design with the blood of the lamb. What the reason for this might be, I will tell in a few words. Hyssop, Palladius, is said to be a herb, and the physicians admire it as well able to melt away, and very vigorously, the impurity in the inward parts, and to thin out thoroughly the clotted masses of phlegm, because of the strength of the natural heat that is in it. So the blood is joined to the hyssop, as I said just now, the type showing us indirectly that the precious blood of Christ frees us not only from corruption but also from all impurity hidden within, and does not let us cool off into sloth, but makes us rather fervent in spirit (Romans 12:11).

And that it is necessary and profitable for those once counted worthy to share in Christ to love to keep the life of holiness secure and never to leave it, the law indicates again by seating within the doors those who had eaten the lamb, so that they might not be destroyed along with the Egyptians by going out of their houses. choices.english: those who have chosen to hold perverted views
choices.why: ἐξίτηλος, faded or degenerate; of doctrine, debased.
The type signifies obliquely, not by plain statement.

choices.english: who has, as a kind of house, … (virtue)
choices.why: The word ἀρετήν is split at the column break; ‘virtue’ is rendered once, at the start of §10.
